props.title: Il Divo

sections.content: Il Divo (2008) revolutionized political biopics with Paolo Sorrentino's hyperstylized portrayal of Italian Prime Minister Giulio Andreotti. Unlike traditional political dramas like The Iron Lady (2011) or Lincoln (2012), Sorrentino crafts a surreal, almost operatic examination of power. The film's baroque visual style and Toni Servillo's unnervingly still performance as Andreotti set new standards for political character studies. It shares DNA with The Conformist (1970) in its examination of Italian political machinery, but pushes further into experimental territory.

sections.content: Sorrentino's approach to political filmmaking influenced a wave of stylized European biopics. Walk the Line (2005) and Ray (2004) played it safe with linear narratives, but Il Divo fragments time and reality to mirror Andreotti's labyrinthine political world. The film's innovative sound design and theatrical staging techniques echo through later works like Jackie (2016) and Spencer (2021), where internal psychological states manifest as bold artistic choices.

The film's examination of Italian political corruption connects to classics like Hands Over the City (1963) and Investigation of a Citizen Above Suspicion (1970). But Sorrentino's postmodern approach - mixing pop music, slow-motion sequences, and surreal imagery - creates something entirely new. This influenced political films like The Young Pope (2016) and Vice (2018), which similarly blend fact and fevered imagination. SUBHEAD: The New Wave of European Political Cinema

sections.content: Il Divo marked a turning point in European political cinema, moving away from straightforward docudrama toward more experimental approaches. Films like The Ghost Writer (2010) and In the Loop (2009) followed suit, using dark humor and stylized presentations to tackle political subjects. Sorrentino's techniques - the fourth-wall breaks, the operatic violence, the dreamlike sequences - created a template for directors seeking to capture political complexity through artistic innovation.
